title: Community Participation Optimizer — Master Tool Specification
description: The complete tool specification: purpose, scope, record layout, and honesty notes.
body: Community Participation Optimizer is entry 986 in the JAH-N Signature catalog of viral-capable AI tools, generators, and simulators, in the Advanced Viral Intelligence and Personalization family. Identifies ways to make a project easier to join, contribute to, remix, and understand. This Signature edition record is the master tool specification: the authoritative description of what the tool does, who it serves, and how it is built. The purpose is shareability by design. Every output is meant to be posted, remixed, challenged over, or built upon with friends, so the specification treats virality as a product requirement: surprise, personalization, competition, creativity, and repeat use. The specification is organized as eight full records. The master record states the purpose and the whole shape of the tool. The input record defines every accepted input. The pipeline record walks the generation stages in order. The programs record names the software, models, libraries, and APIs required, and says honestly which parts run locally and which need a connected model or engine. The outputs record lists every format the tool produces. The sharing record defines export, attribution, remixing, and permissions. The validation record lists the tests the tool must pass. The evolution record maps the ladder from a simple working version to god-mode autonomy. Runtime status is specification: this is a proposed concept and a complete buildable specification, not a running production system. Classification: generator. Like every database in this lane, Community Participation Optimizer is specified as a generator that acts on user-supplied input at runtime; the database itself stores specifications, never anyone's private data.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Input Specification
description: Every accepted input: prompts, files, preferences, assets, and authorized data.
body: The Signature edition input specification for Community Participation Optimizer. Inputs are everything the tool accepts before generation begins: prompts, files, preferences, assets, and authorized data. Accepted inputs: (content_sample: artifact, required) (audience_hints: list, optional) (goal: enum, optional) (constraints: list, optional) (baseline_data: dataset, optional). Required inputs are content_sample; everything else has a working default so the tool runs from a single prompt. Inputs are validated before the pipeline starts: types are checked, text is length-bounded, uploaded assets are scanned for format, and preferences are normalized. Invalid input fails fast with a plain-language message, never a silent wrong result. The demo attached to this record validates a sample input object against the required set and reports exactly which fields passed, so the schema is executable, not just documented.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Generation Pipeline
description: The ordered generation stages from request to packaged output.
body: The Signature edition generation pipeline for Community Participation Optimizer, in execution order. Stage 1, Ingest content and stated goal. Stage 2, Retrieve pattern libraries. Stage 3, Analyze patterns and generate variants. Stage 4, Simulate scenarios with labeled estimates. Stage 5, Validate estimates are labeled, not facts. Stage 6, Package insight report. Each stage has a single responsibility and a checkable output: the parser produces a normalized request, retrieval produces candidate material, generation produces the core artifact, rendering produces the share-ready form, validation produces a pass or fail verdict, and packaging produces the export bundle. A failure at any stage stops the pipeline and reports which stage failed and why, so nothing half-built is ever presented as finished. The pipeline is deterministic for a fixed seed and input: the same seed and topic always produce the same record, which makes results reproducible, testable, and fair in competitive modes. The demo attached to this record walks the stage list, totals the estimated stage costs, and names the bottleneck stage, exercising the pipeline definition as data.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Programs and Dependencies
description: Models, libraries, APIs, and software required, with an honest local-vs-external split.
body: The Signature edition programs and dependencies record for Community Participation Optimizer. Required software: pattern-analyzer.js (runs locally in JavaScript). variant-generator (requires a connected model, API, or engine). scenario-simulator.js (runs locally in JavaScript). estimate-labeler.js (runs locally in JavaScript). The honest split matters. Local JavaScript components run anywhere with no network and no key: parsing, packaging, scoring, layout, and validation. Model-required components need a real model behind them: text generation, image rendering, video planning, and audio. The specification defines their interfaces, inputs, outputs, and fallbacks, but it does not pretend a specification performs the work. The demo attached to this record partitions the dependency list into locally runnable and externally required entries, so the honesty split is computed, not claimed.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Output Formats
description: Every format the tool produces, built for sharing.
body: The Signature edition output formats record for Community Participation Optimizer. Every run produces: insight report, variant set, scenario model, JSON analysis. Outputs are designed for sharing first: sized for common social platforms, captioned in plain language, and bundled so one tap exports everything the result needs to travel. Each output carries attribution to the tool and, where remixed, to the original creator, because viral spread without credit is a bug. Machine-readable JSON ships alongside every human-readable artifact, so results can feed other tools, the boundless generators, and the archive without re-typing. The demo attached to this record enumerates the format list and counts it, proving the output contract is data the system can read.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Sharing and Collaboration
description: Export, attribution, remixing, permissions, and community features.
body: The Signature edition sharing and collaboration record for Community Participation Optimizer. Sharing features: export report, share variants, labeled estimates only, no real user data. Export is one click and includes the artifact, its caption, its attribution, and its license, so nothing shared loses its provenance. Remixing is allowed with attribution; the remix chain is preserved so a group can see how an idea evolved from person to person. Permissions are explicit and creator-controlled: public, friends-only, or private, with community features gated on opt-in. Attribution is automatic, not optional, and every share states plainly whether the content is AI-generated, fictional, or a labeled estimate. The demo attached to this record computes the permission matrix from the license, showing export, attribution, remix, commercial, and privacy rules as data.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Validation Plan
description: Tests for correctness, usability, safety, and output quality.
body: The Signature edition validation plan for Community Participation Optimizer. Every record must pass: schema check. predictions labeled estimates. no guaranteed outcomes. no personal data used. Validation runs at three levels. Schema validation rejects malformed records before they are stored. Usability validation checks that outputs render, read cleanly, and work on a phone. Safety validation checks labeling: fiction is labeled fiction, estimates are labeled estimates, and nothing is presented as a completed product when it is a proposed concept. Verification status on these records is proposed: the specification is complete and the demos execute, but the tool as a whole awaits a tested implementation before any stronger claim is made. The demo attached to this record runs the record validator against a synthetic record and reports the verdict, so the validation logic itself is exercised.

title: Community Participation Optimizer — Evolution Ladder
description: The progression from simple to god-mode, rung by rung.
body: The Signature edition evolution ladder for Community Participation Optimizer. As the generator runs, it progresses: simple: a single working input-to-output path. competitive: a fair scoring or comparison layer. mix-and-match: swappable parts and variant mixing. unmade: ideas never built before. top-notch-or-better: beating the best public alternative. future-grade: speculative next-generation capability. god-mode: open-ended autonomous operation. The ladder is a build discipline, not marketing. Each rung is only claimed when it is demonstrated: simple means one path works end to end; competitive means scoring is transparent and fair; mix-and-match means parts compose without breaking; unmade means the output is genuinely new; top-notch-or-better means it beats the reference; future-grade means it reaches beyond current practice; god-mode means it operates open-endedly within its bounds. The hard cap is one quadrillion records; the generator refuses more. The demo attached to this record emits the full ladder with each rung's focus, so the progression plan is executable data.
